newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks touch new highs, end at record close.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks touch new highs, end at record close.

text.p: Swiss shares again finished at a record close on Thursday after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) touched an all-time high at 4,836.1 points during the session on average volume.
The positive interest rate environment, a somewhat firmer dollar, technical factors and options-related trading supported the market, dealers said.
The SMI finished up 1.15 percent or 55 points at 4,836.1. The all-share Swiss Performance Index added 0.93 percent or 28.26 points to finish at 3,051.18.
Wall Street's higher opening sparked a rally toward the close of the session, dealers said.
Pharmaceuticals Roche and Novartis were volume leaders.
Novartis, which will pay its dividend on Friday, met solid demand. The stock jumped 39 francs or 2.07 percent to 1,923 francs, Roche rose 105 francs or 0.86 percent to 12,305.
Cyclical share Clariant moved within the market trend and rose 1.09 percent to 834 francs.
Speculation that Alusuisse could sell its Lonza division to Ems Chemie helped to push prices higher, although one dealer said such a deal was unlikely to happen.
Alusuisse rose 14 francs to 1,235, while Ems jumped 30 francs to 6,030.
Swiss Re again profited from analysts' recommendations and from its plan to spin off its Alternative Risk Transfer activities into a separate legal unit. Shares advanced 32 francs to 1,661.
Soffex trade saw a slight ease in volatilities as investors took profits on options, dealers said. Overall trade was quiet.
The SMI index futures traded slightly above its fair value, dealers said. The May SMI closed 28 points higher at 4,770.
